summary: Completed the bounded product/frontend source review of cb438d1083e9ae3e2a38dd8e5d7dba4c778b2e89. Two medium findings: stale live Crosswalk Nexus data and monitoring read failures presented as empty history. One low finding: opening the mobile navigation drawer leaves forward keyboard navigation behind its overlay. Crosswalk and drawer behavior were reproduced in isolated Chromium; the monitoring issue is source-supported only. No high or critical product finding was established.

findings.mechanism: When another user, tab or agent changes a requirement while Crosswalk Nexus remains open, state.updated invalidates state/node/my-work but not crosswalk, crosswalk-rows or crosswalk-threats. The latter keys hold assessment-dependent percentages/statuses and have neither a polling interval nor window-focus refetch. Ordinary live mutations therefore leave the visible Nexus and mapping rows stale until navigation, a full resync or another all-workspace invalidation.
findings.evidence: Runtime-confirmed in browser-review.log (crosswalk-sse): PATCH current=4 returned200; the selected PR.AA group stayed at6 units /0% ready, browserReadsAfterMutation was[], and a fresh crosswalk GET returned readiness0.16666666666666666. CrosswalkPage.tsx:79 and317-318 define the independent keys; main.tsx:15 disables focus refetch. Counterevidence: useWsMutation invalidates the whole workspace for a write initiated in this client, reconnect/workspace.updated invalidates all, and the Matrix refreshes independently every30s; the finding concerns the mounted Nexus during ordinary external changes. See crosswalk-stale.png and source-evidence.log.
findings.recommendation: Include all assessment-dependent Crosswalk query keys in the state/evidence/task/check invalidation paths or consolidate them under a shared invalidation prefix. Add a browser check that updates an assessment through a second request and observes an already-open Nexus group and mapping row update without reload.

findings.mechanism: At narrow widths, opening the navigation drawer changes only navOpen. The nav precedes its trigger in DOM order and focus stays on the trigger, so the next forward Tab skips all newly opened navigation destinations and eventually enters main-page controls behind the pointer-blocking drawer/backdrop. This is a confusing keyboard navigation order for the open drawer. It does not declare modal semantics, and lack of a focus trap alone is not the finding.
findings.evidence: Runtime-confirmed in browser-followup.log (mobile-drawer-tabs): at390x844, Open menu + Enter + Tab moved to Workspace, Search, Account, then the main approval link; inNav remainedfalse for every step, and the main link center was covered by shell__backdrop. Shell.tsx:497-507 renders NavRail before TopBar and main; its nav effects only close on path/Escape/widening. Counterevidence: Shift+Tab can reach the prior nav, Escape closes it, background actions remain keyboard-activatable, and no role=dialog/aria-modal contract is declared. The backdrop is translucent, so the observation does not establish a fully hidden focus component or a WCAG failure. mobile-nav-focus.png was captured during transition and is supporting context only. Severity is low rather than a deployment-blocking accessibility claim.
findings.recommendation: Move focus to the current or first navigation destination when the drawer opens and restore its trigger on dismissal, or arrange the drawer after the trigger in the meaningful tab order. If the drawer is intended to behave modally, declare that behavior and keep background content inert; if nonmodal, ensure forward traversal and dismissal do not leave focus unexpectedly beneath the overlay. Cover the selected model with a narrow-viewport keyboard check.

findings.mechanism: Source-only prediction: if the connectors or checks GET fails on first load, the page discards both query error/loading states by destructuring only data with empty-array defaults. It then displays zero connectors or0/0 checks passing and tells each existing connector to collect its first results. A failed monitoring read is presented as absence of monitoring history, with no alert or retry, even when failed checks already exist.
findings.evidence: EvidencePage.tsx:109-110 drops both query states;169 handles only evidenceQuery.error;199 displays connector/check counts;323 renders the first-results message when results is empty;329 renders No connectors yet. source-evidence.log preserves these excerpts. browser-followup.log establishes the seeded fixture actually had2 connectors,12 checks and1 failure. The attempted injected503 reproduction did not reach assertions because its heading selector was wrong (the actual heading is Evidence ledger); no runtime confirmation is claimed. Counterevidence: evidence metadata and individually deep-linked check dialogs do have explicit error/retry UI; cached prior monitoring data may remain visible after a later failure, but is also not labeled stale.
findings.recommendation: Retain the connector/check query objects and present loading/error/retry independently from their successful empty states. When cached results are shown after a refresh failure, label them stale. Verify initial and background503 paths without losing genuine empty-state behavior.

limitations: This is a bounded product/frontend review, not a security/authentication or operational deployment sign-off. Source files were sampled by the stated journey scope; no claim of exhaustive line-by-line coverage.

The lead owns the full pnpm check and dependency audit; this reviewer did not execute the existing unit/e2e suites or a shared build. Both custom browser scripts exited nonzero after useful observations due review-harness locator mistakes; their logs preserve those failures and must not be represented as passing suites.
Monitoring failure finding is source-supported only. Its attempted runtime assertion was blocked by a wrong heading locator and was not retried beyond the assigned bounded follow-up.

Mobile smoke covered seeded pages at390x844 in Chromium with a resized desktop browser context. It did not exercise every full workflow, native touch browser, screen reader, contrast audit or all viewport sizes. Auditor capture/ZIP and proposal decisions were reviewed in source and existing test coverage, not executed here.

Large-data render behavior was inspected in source but no tenant-scale benchmark, CPU trace, memory profile, Web Vitals measurement or slow-device capacity threshold was established. Full-list Plan/Evidence/Auditor rendering remains a deployment capacity question rather than a supported quantified performance defect.

No service8787 access/writes, external credentials, live tenant writes, product edits, shared builds, subagents or external model calls. All runtime mutations were in a disposable in-memory workspace, deleted after reproduction.
